review_text: My amazing fabulous diva Grandma and I were the only people eating lunch here today aside from Kyra Sedgwick and her Grandma. So, that was already pretty cool. The food here was too good for my vocabulary to do it justice. We shared a lovely salad to begin along with the breadsticks/bread/olives that were set out for us. I had the fig and beet ravioli which was by FAR the best ravioli I've ever had. The portion sizes were perfect and beautifully presented. The service was impeccable. For dessert we shared "all about chocolate" which was exactly what you'd expect. Little did we know, they also brought out adorable little pasties on the house- had we known that we probably would have skipped the chocolate dessert. We are BIG sweets eaters and couldn't make a dent in the spread left for us. All in all, this was one of my favorite dining experiences to date and I would love to go back sometime soon! It is, however, rather pricey- as to be expected with quality and service like this- but definitely worth a special occasion splurge if you've got the money (or a diva Grandma who does :) Bravo! Bravo! Bravo!

Despite having a limited time to make a reservation, the concierge at The Mark came through and managed to squeeze in a party of four on a Saturday night. The wait staff was attentive, but a bit too assertive when it came to taking our seats and reviewing the menu. The restaurant was full, yet there wasn't a wait and it didn't feel congested. The people watching factor is as high as anywhere else I've eaten on the Upper East Side and the food was very good. If the Mark concierge can squeeze me back in, I'll be back!

Beautiful space have eaten here both times with 6 or more people have tried almost every dish for the price nothing ever stood out not the bass or the steak , short ribs. The service good but not friendly. The last time we used the coat check where we also checked some wine glasses in gift bags. When we left the coat check girl never gave us the glasses and we forgot to ask for them. We called 2 days later they said they will hold them for us to pick up. When we showed up 5 days later they said someone must have thrown them out not an apology , free drink nothing, bad, bad form for a place where we dropped at least 2k each time. We're done with this place.

Big power scene...but we had a reservation just before Christmas and when we arrived there was a private party. They wouldn't even let me have a drink while I waited for the other 3 in my party to arrive. Go there if you're a bigwig or if you have a healthy ego and want to pay a lot to pretend you are.

Gorgeous, intimate space on the UES with excellent food.  Decor is outstanding particularly when one considers the size of the restaurant.  Of course, being in NY, means you should make a rez or be okay sitting in the front room near the bar.  

Service is outstanding as well and the wine list is a bible.

In summary, one of the best places in the neighborhood.

Went for a glass of wine, MAYBE a salad... 5 glasses of wine and six courses later, I was in Italian heaven. Gazpacho tea cup, broccoli puree soup, tuna tartare, lobster entree, sorbet, italian donuts filled with ricotta -- un. real. he faces on the wall are a little weird, gives you something to talk about and remember. Bit stuffy for me, definitely a mature crowd. Service is OUTSTANDING. The bartender Theodora was a gem. Not just dining out -- it's an experience.

I went on a Wednesday night with my dad and aunt. It was a very mellow and upscale atmosphere with a bit of an older crowd. I was seated at the first table in the dining area, closest to the bathroom with my back to the rest of the restaurant, so I wasn't starting at the older folks and didn't have to look at the slightly creepy wall of faces that's painted on their back wall. I had a much beter view of the super cute hostess instead. 

The service was decent, they didn''t come check on you very often, but were available to be flagged down quite easily. Good if you aren't in a rush and just wanted to enjoy each course at your own pace. 

I started with the assorted meats (delicious), had the lobster main course (amazing), and fresh doughnuts for dessert which they wheel out on a cart so you can see. The caramel/maple dipping sauce was incredible combined with the doughnuts. It wasn't a very novel dessert since I've had similar amazing freshly made doughnuts before at other restaurants like this (Perilla) but a good dish is a good dish. 

Great grappa selection as well, had a super sweet Amarone which I had never tried before. They had mostly grape distilled, very smooth grappas. 

I wuold definitely reccomend this place for a date, special occasion or just a nice dinner to treat yourself to!

Truly one of the best Italian restaurants I've ever experienced. My taylor for my wedding dress is located down the block. My fiance, mother, sister and myself were starving and came across this place. First we sat by the bar had a glass of wine, which was out of sight. We glanced at the menu and thought "Expensive yes, but let's give it a try". A few hours later we were in Italian heaven! To start we ordered oysters, an antipasti dish, and asparagus. For our entree I went with homemade fettuccine, with a cream sauce and to top it off they had black truffles, never tasted anything like it in my life, my fiance had lobster and my mom and sis went with the crab ravioli. To the end night we had cappuccinos, along with Chocolate cake, sorbet, and ricotta stuffed pastries. This restaurant was a real treat for all of us! 

The staff was incredibly friendly and sweet. The ambiance was beautiful.

I went here with my friend from California who was staying at the Surrey Hotel nearby.  I can't believe I had not tried this restaurant sooner as it is only a few blocks away from my house.  The food is just delicious and the decor and service is very good as well.  The waiters are friendly and helpful and I had fun practicing my Italian with them.  My favorite dish was the Farfalle  con Vellutata di Parmigiano, Pomodoro, e Tartufo  Nero (Bowtie pasta in a creamy Parmesan sauce with fresh tomatoes and black truffles) a decadent dish but so worth it!! I highly recommend it!  We went back twice in one week because it was so good!

This is a great, formal, UES neighborhood restaurant. Maybe too formal for its own good. I dont have any negative things to say but be prepared that the average age is 55+ in the dining room. Its not a cool hip spot, a better place to take your parents or have a business meeting. The specials are better than the menu options in my view. The regulars always get priority seating if there is a wait. Highlights include the beet salad, the veal chop, the organic chicken, and the steak. The wait staff is well trained and hard working.

The minute you walk into Caravaggio, an aroma of fresh truffles greets you and follows you into the absolutely gorgeous dining room.  Located in close proximity to some of the best art museums in the country, Caravaggio takes this inspiration and displays modern sculpture and murals throughout the breathtaking restaurant. What also amazed me was the sound architecture in the main dining room - although every table was filled, we were able to carry out intimate dining conversation without shouting over everyone else.  

Now on to the food. We had an italian sausage and buffala mozzarella antipasti and both were amazing.  The italian sausage was extremely tender and flavorful, and the beets paired nicely with the buffala mozzarella.  But then the pasta really took the cake. We ordered three different pastas to share with the table, and they thoughtfully brought each one of us a plate with a tasting portion of each of the three pastas so that we didn't need to pass around each plate and divvy them up ourselves. We ordered a pesto spaghetti that was a special for the evening, along with a bowtie pasta with a black truffle cream sauce, as well as the cavatelli with jumbo crab meat and fresh sea urchin.  All of the pastas were extremely fresh and perfectly cooked, but I have to say the cavatelli was a bit on the saltier side.

For my entree I had the branzino special served over mushrooms. It came with crispy branzino layers stacked one on top of the other.  It was amazing. I loved the perfectly crispy skin of the branzino. Even though I couldn't finish it, it still tasted great the next day.

The wait staff and service were all excellent. I felt like I was in a real Italian restaurant (I'm pretty sure a requirement for working there is that you're Italian, as everyone seemed to be).  The waiter we had recommended a superb white chardonnay that was one of the best I've ever had. It was light, crisp, and buttery.  The best part was the enormous black truffle they kept in a dome next to our table. They brought it over and let us take in the surreal aroma.

I probably wouldn't go back to Caravaggio on my own dime, I was lucky to have been a guest and so glad our host knew of this special restaurant.

Caravaggio is very pretty inside, smells great, and the staff is professional and attentive.  However the food left a lot to be desired.  The shrimp scampi special was too salty, the farfalle pasta dish had too much garlic, and the risotto with gorgonzola cheese and peas was overpowered by the gorgonzola sauce.  Granted, gorgonzola is a strong cheese, but it could have been balanced out better.  After a strawberry shortcake dessert that fell flat, we were presented with a large bill, that showed that one of our entrees, the crab legs, was $60.  This had been one of the specials, and was twice the price of any other entree on the menu, which the waiter should have told us.  He did hint that the truffle entree special was quite pricey, probably meaning closer to $100, but I think if a special is twice the price of a normal menu item, the waiter should let the diners know.

I know this is a fancy UES restaurant, and I was expecting a large bill, but I was also expecting the food to be delicious and memorable, which is was not.

We came here with friends to celebrate my wife's birthday and had a very memorable restaurant experience. The Peninsula concierge recommended it and arranged the reservation. Walking in you know this will be a first class experience. Interior is similar to decor you might find in a Four Seasons, or Peninsula Hotel- sedate, beautifully designed. The wait staff was very attentive on the evening we were there, the chef even came out to greet our party and speak a little Italian with our friends- nice touch! And the food? Each dish was out done by the next. All in all a 5 star experience, which we felt was worth the high price tag.

The best Italian restaurant that I've been to in New York, and I've been to many. I came here with a group of 7 to celebrate my birthday and had one of the best meals of my life.

Caravaggio is located just off of Madison on 74th with a pretty unassuming entrance, but once you get inside you can tell that it's an upscale place. The decor and atmosphere is artsy without being overdone, and it's surprisingly spacious. Our server was hilarious and very personable, and was actually Italian. Being a classier place, the noise level was pretty quiet and the other diners in the restaurant seemed a little pretentious, but that didn't stop our group from being loud and having a good time.

Words cannot do justice to the food so I won't try. There was not one dish that I did not like out of all the appetizers and entrees that our group of 7 ordered. They even brought us out some complimentary pastries after dinner, which were similarly delicious.

As far as the price, Caravaggio is the perfect place for a special occasion (aka, the $$$$ is NOT an exaggeration). That being said, you certainly get what you pay for.

If someone from out of town was looking for the quintessential Italian restaurant in New York, I'd point them here.

Having read the recent positive posts, we tried Caravaggio and were disappointed. The plates had some good qualities; very fresh ingredients and wonderful presentation but most of them fell very short on flavors. The specials we tried all seemed salty and bland. The 45 dollar Seafood combination featured lobster which had a not so nice frozen taste. We did notice that what was ordered off the menu (and not a special) seemed to be a bit more evolved. (The Branzino had great sweet and salty flavors) Overall though, the food definitely doesn't measure up to the exciting menu and waiter descriptions. Also did not find it to be the friendly atmosphere with great service everyone here spoke of. The army of waiters had undeserving attitude.

Beautiful room, sophisticated ambience, modern art, occasional power players, and fine food make for a special night at Caravaggio,which plays in a certain high end Italian niche you may only find in Manhattan.  

I was impressed with the ambience, professionalism of the staff, and great choices for specials. (Our waiter seemed to remember at least a dozen in great detail, without needing to look at his "cheat sheet.")

Standouts included a grilled sardine appetizer, linguine, and a rich burrata.  

Ambience is a bit formal for my taste, but overall Caravaggio is a highly professional, high quality Italian restaurant that appears perfect for a business dinner or night out with visitors or parents.

We had a lunch at your restaurant last Saturday just after visiting the Metropolitan museum. I was  amazed to see works by Frank Stella  and on the walls. Beautiful setting, fine food and friendly atmosphere!  The wait staff and service were all excellent.

Speaking of disasters...lasts night dinner at a very pricey highly touted Italian restaurant Caravaggio) was a huge disappointment.
The room was beautiful...modern and very well designed. Alice and I shared a pasta to begin with...it was fine...then I ordered Bronzino with an interesting sauce...it was just ok...portion was paltry. Alice ordered a Strip Steak which, when it came out looked beautiful ...artfully arranged with potatoes, etc. She could not slice it without using as lot of force...we call the waiter over...get this...he tells us they're having trouble with their steak knives...so it's not the steak it's the knife?
She ate a few slices and...after what seemed a long while the waiter asks if she would like something else...she had the pasta and did not want anything else....waiter takes the steak away and says nothing. We have so many restaurant we love with great food and no attitude but every other week we try a new place...so far we loved the Mark but disliked 2 others.
Now we are wondering if they are going to charge us for a very expensive but very tough cut of steak and are preparing remarks to show our outrage. I am tough in these situations but Alice goes for the kill.
Bottom line...waiter says nothing hands me the bill...steak was not charged...never said "we will not charge for the steak...sorry you did not like it, can I offer you some wine on the house...no!!!...he offers us expressos. He never smiled throughout the entire dinner even when I suggested that he go into the kitchen and bring out a butcher's saw.

Was there for lunch yesterday with a friend from out of town.  I wanted to treat to a nice Italian place near where they were staying.  However, we were all disappointed.  There were only 3 tables occupied for a 1pm lunch.  The service was beyond slow.  They were attributing to the fact that my daughter ordered risotto which is made from scratch.  I wondered whether they were still on a summer schedule with a very small staff for lunch.  My clam and mussel dish was terrible.  I would normally wouldn't have sent it back as kids were getting restless due to the very very slow service.  But honestly, I couldn't take another bite - bitter!!!  They insisted that I get another pasta entree saying that it would be fast, another 10 minutes.  By then, the check was paid and the pasta was packed to go home.  Yesterday's experience overall was less than a star, but I would like to try once more give that rating.  Would like to come once more when their game is back on.  But again, there are so many great restaurants in NYC, I don't know when I will be coming back to drop another several hundred dollars.

I was very excited to visit this restaurant after reading the great reviews. It seemed like a great place to celebrate our anniversary. We did not, however, have the opportunity to enjoy a meal here. My husband and I arrived at the restaurant and were waiting for our table when a well dressed black foursome arrived at the restaurant. They were told that they would not be welcome in the restaurant due to "improper footwear" and that it didn't meet the dresscode (there is no dress code alluded to on the website). The restaurant representative had not even looked at our manner of dress or footwear. 
I was appalled at this blatant racism in an upscale restaurant and was shocked that I was actually seeing this. The foursome pointed out my husband's footwear at which time the restaurant representative also told us that we wouldn't be able to dine there. An unnecessary message as there was no way that I would be giving any money to an establishment that chooses it's customers by race. Completely inappropriate and downright disgusting.

We were a party of 4 ppl on Wednesday evening, we all agreed this experience was not to be repeated. Bad service, expensive and bland food, the atmosphere of a mausoleum. Of all the good restaurants in NYC, why bother. SKIP!

Remarkable food -- I think there were about 18 dishes that I would have been thrilled to order
Great atmosphere -- you can actually have a conversation
Not your typical Italian -- well worth it

It was very good food but you can get the same food elsewhere for half the price. Maybe this is because I'm not a HUGE fan of italian food. Strong martinis, very disappointing bread basket. They did have a truffle menu ($100-200 per dish) that was excellent (but how could you mess up truffles? they're delicious). Very good service (but expected)

Somebody else was paying but wouldn't come here on my own

Had lunch there recently.  The space while at points rather narrow is nicely appointed with works of art.  The lunch prix fixe at $26 for two courses seemed reasonable and while a couple of the dishes were unavailable when we went, the preparation and presentation were just fine.  A  veal scallopine in a sauce with lemon and artichoke was not too adventurous and the veal pounded into small medallions might be been more tender.  The starter salad with toasted hazelnuts and cheese was perfectly okay.  Their "crudo" app of sashimi looked and tasted fine.  The small dish of olives they served with the bread was very tasty. We did not try any wine.  So, basically aside from the convenient location if you want a quiet meal on the Upper East Side, it's hard to get excited pro or con about the cuisine here.

Loved it. Great food and great service in attractive East Side location. The extensive, interesting menu  will dazzle you. The in season white truffles had an awesome aroma. I felt like I was in a first class, authentic restaurant in Italy. The small eat-in bar was humming on a Sunday night.

Like fellow Yelpers... this italian restaurant left me stale (like the bread)  that was served to us..  I think for the price, it could have done better..  I have eaten at Del Posto and it was incredible..  and a few mom and pop places (which it truly amazing)  

I would not come back..  Sorry

The decoration is chic and modern, with artworks very tastefully arranged. I thought I was in for an amazing dinner.

Unfortunately, the food was very mediocre. The pasta and fish entrees both had fancy names but bland flavors. The salad and butternut squash soup were better, but still not impressive. 

The servers at the table were prompt and didn't let my wine glass empty (always a plus). The other staff though, like the hosts, were standoffish...

Caravaggio is definitely a nice dinner spot, so I wouldn't swing by to grab drinks and enjoy the atmosphere. I'm not sure in what situation I'd come back here, given the disappointing experience with the food.

I really wanted to give Caravaggio 4 stars. Before trying this place I read a few negative Yelp reviews and thought perhaps Yelpers were being overly critical. 

But it's true, everything on the menu sounds so much more beautiful than it tastes. And for the slightly higher price they charge per dish compared to other great Italian restaurants in the area, you would think there'd be an extra WOW factor. 

Unfortunately not. 

AMBIANCE:
Contemporary, sophisticated design, a tad-bit stuffy with quite a number of men wearing jackets. The wall at the back of the restaurant is plastered with basic sketches of people's faces with their mouths open (interesting?). Like a 6 year old designed the wall. 

FOOD:
Bread baskets for me are key and can make or break my experience. Caravaggio served a semi-warm bread basket with about 3-4 selections. Coupled with olive oil and balsamic vinegar. Each table also has a standing basket of breadsticks. It wasn't bad, but i've had more exciting bread baskets. 

Now the two highlights for me were the amuse bouche and my warm octopus salad appetizer. 

The amuse bouche was a fried risotta croquetta on creamy tartar sauce. It was delicious! Great start to the meal. 

BEST DISH OF THE NIGHT - the warm octopus salad. I almost always get the octopus salad at every italian restaurant I dine at and i've had some amazing ones. Caravaggio's octopus salad was definitely a winning dish. The vegetables were all cooked in a warm broth and topped with slices of juicy octopus. Very hearty dish that held up the entire meal. 

For my main, I tried two pastas - the oriechette with sausage and broccoli rabe and the meat ragu with fettucine and peas. I was slightly disappointed. I like my pastas to taste home-cooked and hearty. These pastas just didn't hit that target. The oriechette pasta was on the dry side, and the ragu was just A-OK. Nothing to crow about, i didn't even finish my dish. 

DESSERT:

I tried the apple tart a la mode and the chocolate hazelnut mousse cake. Both dishes were solid and my sister who is a dessert fanatic thoroughly enjoyed them. I am picky about my apple tarts and the one served here had a lovely flaky crust. Only wish the scoop of vanilla ice-cream was larger. Ask for two scoops so that you can have consistent bites of ice-cream and apple tart. 

At the end of the meal, it was a nice treat to get complimentary petit fours that comprised a selection of biscottis and one macaroon. I'm not a huge fan of biscotti or macaroon, so I have not much to comment on this. 

OVERALL:
I have no qualms paying a premium for good food. However, the only dish I tried at Caravaggio that was value for the quality was their warm octopus salad. Every other dish was surprisingly underwhelming. I really did expect better from this place seeing as the items on the menu looked so tasty. Note to Yelpers: Try Felidia instead on 58th between 2nd and 3rd. You won't be disappointed.

The breadsticks here were the best part of my meal. Those things are about as long as a person's forearm. And they're nice and crunchy and I swear they must lace it with crack because I am usually so controlled around that sort of stuff. Not this time though; I probably had about six or seven breadsticks before we were even served drinks.

The wine was also yummalicious, but my uncle got a few of their most expensive bottles of white and red, so there you go. Initially the waiters were slow in refilling, but once the meal commenced, my glass was always full. So my initial frustration was replaced with a nice and happy buzz.

As for the actual food? Totally not worth the price when there are so many other Italian restaurants in the city that serve better food at cheaper prices. Hell, just go to Eataly and you'll get fresher and tastier cheeses and pastas that are cooked al dente.

Their fresh buffalo mozzarella was okay, but didn't blow me away like some places. My uncle loved it, but he was also well on his way to getting drunk.

I ordered the homemade penne in tomato sauce with melted mozzarella on top. It was essentially a penne alla vodka, and a bland one at that. The top pieces of penne were dried out and cracked. They were tough to chew. And this is my opinion of it with three glasses of wine in me. Usually I'm a lot more appreciative of food when I've got booze in my system, but an Italian cannot overlook poorly prepared pasta. And it was NOT al dente. More on the mushier side. I think the only redeeming part of my dish was the broccoli rabe that came as a side and the partially burnt mozzarella (I like my cheeses when they're browned and crunchy). The broccoli rabe was sautéed and spicy. My grandpa stole the rest of my side when I wasn't looking. 

Speaking of my grandpa, we came here for his birthday. The staff gave us all tiramisu for dessert and everyone at the table polished it off (again, there was a lot of booze). I had about two spoons of it. I'm not sure what it was about the dessert, but I was not a fan. It, too, was bland in taste. the mouthfeel wasn't very appealing either. They also gave us three plates of cookies. Nobody touched them, but I tried one of the macarons. It wasn't bad, but it was stick to your teeth chewy. 

This place is great if you get their private room. There's lots of artwork to look at while you're chatting with friends and family. The lighting is on the dimmer side, which lends to the intimate atmosphere. I think this place would be nice for a few drinks...not so much for food.

Waitstaff was attentive, which is why I'm giving this place 2stars instead of 1. The food though...the food just did not live up to the fancy names or the price.
Seriously mediocre food, with some things outright bad.  Extraordinarily overpriced.

so good  deserts
Food was just okey , risotto turned out not very tasty , but service was exceptional 
Id like to come back to this place and try something else maybe pasta will be good :)
I originally came here to drink tea with desert and it was just delicious , creamy . Tasty right amount of sugar  and fruits 
Bravissimo

This is close to our hotel so thought we'd try it. Overall the food was a cut above most Italian. The service started out five star but once our entrees were delivered we were abandoned by wait staff. Dropped three bills without wine so expected better.

I am a frequent dinner because of business entertainment.  I had not heard of  Caravaggio but was excited when I read a review in NYT'S and decided to take clients there.

What a disappointment!  Although the restaurant looked nice and the staff pleasant, the food was not up to even a minimum standard.  There were 4 of us and we all had issues with our meal.  We started with a pasta course that was undercooked, the pasta was not al dente but HARD.  Two of us then had a veal chop that was overcooked and had a cardboard texture; my two other guests had fish that was also severely overcooked and dry.

With three bottles of wine, I spent over $1,100 and was very disappointed.  Maybe it was just an off night but I'm not willing to risk it,

We have gone there in the past, the kitchen is normally superb, and we have always  enjoyed ourselves. We decided to go Saturday night and it was a disaster.  The restaurant owners were obviously nowhere to be found, as the bartenders invited their families with children to sit at a bar table, after 9:00pm.  The noise was obnoxious and no one seemed to care; they were actually playing cards!  The food was second rate that night as well. The primary chef must have had the day off. For example, the bibb lettuce salad on the regular menu, usually very elegant, was poorly torn and weighted down with too much greasy dressing.  Completely unlike the regular weekday version.
A great restaurant, but on Saturday nights it's a pass.
This is an incredible restaurant.  Chef Marco is extremely talented. The service was outstanding.  The ambiance was interesting and beautiful.  This is my favorite nyc restaurant.

took my parents visiting from Europe upon Carlyle Hotel recommendations.  This was the most embarrassing dinner in years.  The food is very unremarkable and overpriced but the quality of service is deplorable.  I don't blame the server who had obviously no clue of high dining service but the management who clearly never trained their staff properly.
The server consistently interrupted our conversations to share her/ his opinion or make small talks about Europe and Europeen food (!).
I did not want to post a review at first, because I will never go back anyway but I thought i was necessary to do so that other people do not get hammered with an outrageous bill and a bad experience.

I've been to this restaurant twice; once on business and once  personally, (this past Friday night). Perhaps there aren't many restaurants that are prettier, as sophisticated in design or as relaxing but unfortunately that's where it begins and ends, as both the food and service are completely inconsistent. I've had dishes that were great and others that were terrible, bordering on inedible. At these prices every dish should be a 10 !  
On Friday night, after having an unexpectedly large lunch, I began with the asparagus soup, which was so tiny and bland!!! There might have been less than a half  of a cup of soup, which arrived barely warm, $22.00!!!!! As a second I had the appetizer "special" tuna hamachi which was paired with tuna tartare $32.00!!, a staple that appears on many, many menus around town. I would say there was about a tablespoon of tartare, which was very dark in color and extremely fishy tasting and again very underseasoned. I had to send this back and they replaced it with MORE hamachi. The first round of hamachi which I barely touched had a decent amount of a citrus sauce on it, which covered up again the very fishy flavor and it was sliced way, way too thick. This should NOT be on the menu as a "special" as it was NOT done right. My Mother on the other hand had a spectacular dish of pasta and this has always been my experience here, one thing great, one thing terrible.  
But the reason why I'm giving two stars is because as the night wore on the service really fell off. No one cared that I didn't care for my dish. The owner was there, very grim, walking around the dining room, impossible to get a smile and running it as a "business", which is a feeling I hate. The tuna should have been taken off of the bill, it wasn't.  
So to summarize this review, if you want to pay to sit in a BEAUTIFUL, relaxing room, unlike most of the restaurants in NYC, and are ok paying just to sit in this room, then you can justify the cost factor. But if you are measuring what's on the plate to what's coming out of your pocket, you must skip this restaurant. 
Might I also mention, this review will NOT deter business because the restaurant is comprised of mostly older, well-heeled, upper east siders who don't know much about food and are happy with a piece of fish in their plate and some veggies.

We love Carravagio and have eaten there at least ten times. Not sure why some folks dis the place. We have eaten at tons of great restaurants all over the culinary world and this place delivers. Plus they serve late. Want dinner at 11:30pm this place will accomodate you. Try the Vitello Tonato try the veal scallopine try the white truffles if u feel like. letting out some shaft the tri colore salad rocks too. We are pretty spoiled and we found the service just fine so go figure. The lunch fixed price is a great deal because they do smaller potions baking three courses reasonable. In short go and eat at the bar if it is full. This place is on Madison not out on the avenues. Enjoy

WORST SERVICE EVER. A group of friends from all over the country met in NY for 3 days of great food and fun.  We selected Caravaggio for one of our dinners. There were 13 of us. Bill was $2,000. We ate  in their private dining room. Food was fine but service was the worst we have ever experienced.  the waiters were rude and arrogant. Very disappointing and so uncalled for.  We had to get up and find someone to pour wine, ask for menus, just terrible. Any other restaurant we would have had at least 2 waiters assigned to a party this size. It really was a joke.

Great meal from start to finish. We had a drink while waiting for the rest of our party and they had a mice variety of drink specials to enjoy. At the table the service was prompt but you weren't made to feel rushed. After dinner they let us sit and enjoy dessert and drinks and again didn't make us feel rushed. A wonderful experience and we can't wait to return.

Went there last night for  the first time w my old boss.  Made a 730 reservation.  Was told that it would be a few minutes.  45 minutes later after complaining a few times we were finally seated. Hostess did buy us a round of drinks but like "Seinfeld" said they know how to make a reservation they just don't know how to hold the reservation.  

Service was ok and the food was good not great.  Heirloom tomato salad appetizer was $25.00.  Tasty and different but not worth $25.00. Sea bass was best dish good sauce.   Pasta was mediocre.   Wives split pasta dish.  They charged $40.00 for the split one and charged $30.00 for the one that wasn't split. 

Extra charge showed up on bill called "open food item" no explanation. $16.00. 

Decor is very very nice.  Nice little bar area and beautifully done. However I won't go back. There are plenty of neighborhood Italian places that are better cheaper quieter than this one

A group of friends and I went for a special luncheon and were so very disappointed. The help was UNPLEASANT, RUDE and UNAVAILABLE for very long stretches of time. Never a smile, just growling angry faces. We went during restaurant week and wonder if that is the reason we were treated so poorly. One had a chipped plate, one thought the cold vegetable soup was out of a can and terrible - when told the m'aitre d, all he said was "really?" When the time came for the check, it had an extra drink on it. When we questioned it, we were told "How can I see the right number, there are so many dishes on the table?" The dishes took forever to be cleared. When asked if he could do something to compensate all of our trouble, he said' "Don't come back!!!!" WHOLE EXPERIENCE VERY UNPROFESSIONAL! He made a big thing about changing the check, took over 45 minutes and then charged one of us the total for the table and the others the new corrected amount. Glad she noticed and did not sign. NEVER HAD A WORSE DINING EXPERIENCE.

I can't believe I am writing this review. I went to Caravaggio today for lunch with a group of 30. The food was fair, not great but the service was terrible.
They were short handed but did know in advance we were coming. The service was slow and the attitude of the maitre d was uncaring when we complained. I have never had such poor service. Paying $42 for lunch when 4 of the 6 choices choices were pasta is not a way to get repeat business. I would not recommend this place.

Wait, is that Barbara Walters sitting at the next table? 

Why yes, it is. The fact that the queen of talk news was sitting at the next table underscores how I feel about this place. Just not necessary. For me. 

Caravaggio, I'm so sorry. I had a nice meal and the service was excellent, if a bit over the top. But I'm not a fancy guy and your restaurant was a bit too much for me. It's not your fault. I was invited. It was my uncle's fault, really. 

And your food was really good. I started with the Calamari Salad, which was served sauteed and fresh and topped with a red wine vinaigrette. It was a winner. 

For my main, I had the linguini with clams -- a basic dish done right and to perfection. No complaints here. My fellow diners also did well, with a few people ordering the free range chicken and the red snapper. 

But still our meal felt odd and I think it's because we didn't belong here. I don't need to see Barbara while I'm eating. With all due respect, it's just not my crowd.

If I'm being honest, I'm most comfortable in my sweats, eating pizza, accompanied with a glass of sangria (really not a beer person).  

But every so often, who doesn't love to get wined and dined?  This is where my fiancé and I love to go. (He even proposed here!) The staff greets you upon entering and every single person has a smiling face.  

The food is PHENOMENAL.  Don't even look at the menu and trust the chef.  He will knock your socks off.  I didn't think I could get stuffed off of such small dishes-sorry, but the pricier the meal, the less the give you. But, the quality of food is well worth the price.  

Overall, a great eating experience. Caravaggio, we'll be back!

Perfect service. Very attentive and super professional. The food was amazing. A perfect lunch. Even had a celeb dining two tables away. No big fanfare for the celeb and no  interruption to our dining experience.

I don't understand why this restaurant has only 3 1/2 stars?? The food it's absolutely amazing!!! The soup of the day which was a carrot pure was absolutely delicious. Their pastas and steaks absolutely amazing!! And omg the desserts, a panacotta which was a amazing and the best of the best was the pistachio cake covered in chocolate, YUM!!!! 

The service was super friendly. The atmosphere were mostly older rich people. A lot of old ladies that look like Betty White lol, we were the only young couple. 

I will definitely be returning if I'm in the mood of EXCELLENT Italian food and desserts :)
A nice restaurant with a very attentive service, ambiance is quite and nice, you can have a talk. Food is great, my red snapper was special and the tiramisu, as expected, great.

For my birthday dinner last night, I decided to go to Caravaggio who has a wonderful dessert :malasadas in New York! (Caravaggio's name is Bomboloni)  It cannot beat Malasadas at Leonard's Bakery in Honolulu, but I only can get it at Caravaggio in New York City. 

Food here is always good. But  yesterday's dish I ordered was exceptionally good.  Soft shell crab!  And their service is impeccable.  Sophisticate decoration for beautifully dressed people.   

Rich Upper East Sider's gem. Price is reasonable for this food, services.  For two : $160 (without alcohol) + tip

Disaster! While I have always enjoyed this local gem since Coco Pazzo left the upper East side, I was so disappointed the last time I had dinner there.  The service was terrible and the owner made no attempts to apologize.  In addition, it is now popular with groups, very loud groups. When guests at other tables turned to signal to the group they were loud they only got louder. The staffs response was they will leave soon. Needless to say they were still there when I left. Unfortunate to loose such a local since there are so few choices on the upper east side.
Had the perfect lunch there. Beautiful art works on the walls, and beautiful patrons. Yoko Ono came in just as we were leaving ...

Excellent, excellent, excellent! The service, the food and the atmosphere was incredible. I had one of the specials the evening we dined at Caravaggio and it was impeccable. The staff was very knowledgable about what type of wine worked well with my delicious meal. The desserts were to die for- mouth watering! I highly recommend this delicious Italian beauty!
Taken  here for a  private work lunch the foods good can't speak on the service , The decor is Wacky A+ for that

Reading the menu, I must say was not inspiring, 'seen it ate it' combination of food, but that being said, they do those basic/traditional very well. The wine, the food was delicious, no complaints. Only thing haunting me is their wall art.

Service was excellent.  We were only one of 4 tables seated that night so it felt like there was a whole team of waitstaff attending to our every need. 
We had the duck appetizer and it was the best duck I've ever had.  We all ordered pasta entrees and everyone loved their dishes.  
The place is very expensive but they do back up the price with service and quality.  
Decor was nice too.  The scene is definitely upper east side elite

Wonderful restaurant with a great atmosphere, impeccable service and outstanding food. And they serve dinner later. 

The atmosphere. Wonderful.

The service. The most attentive service. We had several servers attending to our every need from food ordering, clearing dishes immediately upon finishing, and filling our waters and drinks.  In fact, while I can never complain about outstanding service, it was so attentive that there were a couple times I thought I could use a little less attention so that I could have a little more time for uninterrupted conversation. That is not a complaint- I was more humored that the service was so outstanding. 

The food.  Their special list cited by the server was extensive. They served a small cup of cauliflower soup and a truffle flavored encrusted little ball in bit of sauce- on a lovely presented small plate ... A fabulous start to the meal and showcasing the start of a fantastic presentation of all the dishes. We then had the Brussel sprout appetizer from the specials menu - the best Brussel sprout dish I've ever had. Mixed with walnuts and some other ingredients and bursting with perfect flavor.  

They have four fish entrees on the menu plus one or two on their special list, including Bronzino, scallops and swordfish. I ordered the Bronzino which was perfectly presented with colorful mixed vegetables and a light sauce on the side. Absolutely delicious, light, perfect;  the best Bronzino I've had but unfortunately, a couple bones... They kindly took it back to address but I found another - I understand the need to ensure presentation isn't compromised ... They  offered  another entree; so I went with the scallops in a truffle oil. When I commented I loved truffle oil, the server returned to the table with extra truffle oil which he drizzled over my scallops. Perfect !

 Highly recommend.

Saturday night with friends. 8 pm reservation. 
3/4 of the tables seated were on dessert (apparently having enjoyed an imaginary early bird special).

There were many, many specials. An overwhelming amount, and all with complexities. (of the 'dusted with white truffles and chestnut' variety). The wine list was huge, but all hugely overpriced. 

Ended up with burrata (nice, light and well seasoned) and a wonderful lamb ragu over pasta. 

Service was terrific, as noted, but there were several items out on the menu. Not the waiter's fault but still.. 

It was a lovely dinner but truly in the dining environment we are in today, not worth the price. Oh, and by 10-10:30 there were about 5 tables left seated.

Over rated...Do not waste your time and hard earned money.  Have dined at Carvaggio several times, each time, unimpressed.  Now I understand why!  See the below story....

On our recent visit, one of the plates was not as expected and we discussed with the waiter who promptly offered a replacement.  (The service is always excellent, staff is pleasant, eager and responsive to your every request.)

A few minutes later, comes a poorly attired, unkept man in his mid fifties who begins to berate my wife for her feedback of the dish.  He begins a diatribe regarding the city and the Department of Health.  His tone, demeanor and loud voice made our table and the 5-6 tables adjacent to ours extremely uncomfortable.  The man goes on to justify his words and behavior because he is the 'owner'.   
The waitstaff apologized profusely and explain that he is an 'Italian Alpha Male' and very difficult to work with.  Adjacent diner were shocked, having seen the owner's behavior.

So now we know.  Organizations, including restaurants, are only as good as the leader.  
In the case of Carvaggio, a brusque, rude, arrogant owner who mistreats his employees and patrons.

If you value overpriced food in a uncomfortable environment, go visit Carvaggio.  Otherwise, visit the hundreds of other excellent restaurants in  NYC !

Just walked out of the restaurant after waiting over an hour for our first course to arrive (we ordered three). A unique experience in a high end restaurant. Wait staff was clueless. No one seemed to be in charge. Maybe it was Saturday Night Fever.
Good food and adequate service, but they over-charged us, and refused to resolve the issue.  Easily rectified with a substantially reduced tip - but I'd avoid this place.

Had lunch with a large group and the service and food were outstanding, I highly recommend this restaurant. The only draw back is that the wines (nice and large selection) are overpriced and in organizing the event there was little willingness to seek or offer a solution

Appetizer:  Disappointing.
Main course:  Pretty good
Dessert:  Best part of my meal

Came here with a group to have dinner.  The atmosphere screams wealthy Upper East Side.  I think I was the youngest person there too.  Everyone seemed to be an AARP member or someone right around the corner from becoming one.  But I digress.  

Once we've had a chance to settle in and order beverages, the waiter comes over and begins his 10 hour soliloquy on the specials for the night.  Seriously, it felt like the specials list was longer than the actual menu.  For the appetizer - asparagus with fried egg and shaved black truffles.  When I was actually served the dish, I didn't realize it was literally asparagus with fried egg and shaved truffles.  Three limp stalks of asparagus topped with a fried egg (like you get in a diner) and shaved black truffles.  Not a hint of salt anywhere on the dish.  No technique that went into producing good asparagus or a well cooked egg.  No black pepper.  Nothing.  Literally three ingredients on a plate.  It was bland, flavorless and god only knows how much it was (work dinner so I didn't pay).  By far one of the saddest dishes I've ever eaten.  

For the entree, I ordered the cod with clams in lemon sauce.  For a fish dish at a restaurant like this, it wasn't bad.  Well cooked but overly salted here for my taste.  The lemon sauce could have been more lemony and the wilted lettuce added nothing to the dish.  Decent but nothing to write home about.

For dessert, I had the Oops! Tart is Dropped.  Nice balance of sweet, tart, savory.  I liked the freeze dried berries to go along with fresh ones.  The hazelnut tart had enough bite and crunch to complement the other components of the dish.  After a disappointing start to the meal, I was happy to have had this.  

In a city with so many options, I don't think I could ever justify coming here on my own dime, nor would I suggest others to spend their money on me here.

If you are very old, and like a very slow and boring service, this is the place , we had 3 course menú , and  between each plate you have To wait long time To Eat , they need a new host.... Why in upper east side, most restaurantes aré so boring and s0 expensive...

We had a truly amazing dining experience! The food was incredible and the staff was very attentive to making our visit unforgettable! The Experience was complimented with the detailed attention of the Chef! We can't wait to our next visit..

I had the gnocchi and fall salad - both of which are incredibly delicious. The atmosphere was perfect. Why didn't they get 5 stars? 

When we made the reservations its was a 50$ per person fee to cancel, and they emphasized not being late multiple times at the risk of loosing our table. We arrived early and were seated at the bar until the table was ready. 

30 minutes past our reservation we checked in with the staff and they were very rude as if we weren't waiting. 

We sat 40 minutes after our reservation. 

The food saved the place. Absolutely delicious!!! The atmosphere was cozy and we spent three ours eating and drinking.

Beautiful restaurant. Delicious food. Horrible waiter. Rude! Rushing us before we even sat down in a half empty restaurant. 
Have eaten here dozens of times and had wonderful, polite service. This waiter was condescending, impatient, snarky! Ruined our dinner. Will not be back.

Tucked away in the upper east side, this high end Italian restaurant will leave you smiling and satisfied.  Excellent pasta, large portion of osso buco, and extensive wine list.  The dining area is intimate yet not overcrowded.  Service is attentive and knowledgeable.  A pleasant experience in a fancy neighborhood.

This restaurant is one of the best restaurants I have eaten. Food, service, ambiance are outstanding. We had black spaghetti with frutti di mare and black sea bass with chanterelle mushrooms. Both beautifully done. The tiramisu was an experience we never had before. This place offers no pretence, real, outstandingly cooked food with real portions and ethereal, sofisticated, flavors that explode in your mouth.

There are no "off nights" at this place....because it is ALWAYS garbage.  The owner Giuseppe Bruno is perhaps the rudest, most self-important and obnoxious proprietor on the UES...total jerk to all (even regulars such as my family).  Food is nothing more than average.  Often customers will wait ages for food that has clearly been sitting under a heat lamp while inattentive servers lollygag around.  SKIP IT AT ALL COSTS!!!!  

Do yourself a favor and go to Sette Mezzo or Vico for UES Italian food instead...or better yet go right across the street to Come Primo.  You'll be treated better and have better food at each of these altertative establishments.  And you won't have to deal with owner Giuseppe Bruno...who is a total jerk to all!!!!
Caravaggio is an amazing Italian restaurant on the upper East Side.  Exceptional service, beautiful decor, and absolutely delicious food.  Everything was top notch.  Can't wait to go back there.

They try so hard to be a good "upscale" fancy restaurant.... but they are just an average place where dinosaurs dump their money.
Service is slow and stuffy.
Bad experience and empty waller

Anyone looking to have a small wedding in New York City, I highly recommend Caravaggio for your reception dinner!

I had my wedding in Central Park, it was a small wedding and I was looking for a nice restaurant with a private area to hold my reception. This place did not disappoint. The amazing Selby helped me arrange everything from flowers to my cake and it was such an easy, seamless process. My cake (a cupcake tier), was exactly as I wanted it and was soooo delicious. The service on the night was outstanding and the food was so perfect. Thank you all for making the night so wonderful, I couldn't have asked for more.

One of our favorite meals. Impeccable service. Wonderful atmosphere.  We loved the art on display. Our food was crisp and light, yet very flavorful. This will be on list to eat at every time we visit NYC.

One of my favorite places on UES. You'll be hard pressed to find a better dinner. Make sure to try the specials they change all the time. Also they have a wonderful wine list and they make a mean martini. Truly the definition of hand made italian food, they take the time to make it right.
A very old fashion Italian restaurant. Over priced, Half of the food were average, but some of them are very good. I Will not go back again.

Recently dined in this gourmet Italian and am giving it the coveted five star rating for several reasons. The service and the ambiance easily achieve five star treatment. The list of specials is enormous (you really don't need the menu). To quote a long gone friend in a quality establishment you never can go wrong with the specials. Whatever you choose will be well prepared and beautifully plated. But I will only be able to dine here on special occasions as the prices put quite a dent in my modest purse! That being said if price is no object treat yourself to an awesome dining experience at Caravaggio.

The portions are hearty, food was really fantastic, service was attentive but a bit slow. Seated at 8:30 and didn't get our main course until 10. My steak was cool perfectly and the soufflé was wonderful!

I went to this place for dinner with my family on a recommendation from my hotel, The Mark. I loved the decor and the atmosphere. The issue I had was with staff. After getting the NY Strip for my guests (that was extremely Chewy and undercooked) I was told that I should bring it home and that "they have the best steak in NYC".......which they don't. We graciously asked them to take it back and ordered another main course. Upon doing so they added the original order onto the bill. When asked they apologized and came back with the same bill and said there was nothing they could do about it.

Sadly I will say that for this reason I will never recommend this to anyone I know. I guess this restaurant feels that the holiday season brings suckers they can rip off.!
Excellent service and exceptional food! The art mural makes for the perfect back drop when you dine.

Beautiful interior,excellent drinks, delicious food, and great attentive service, what more could you ask for? Portions large, delicious bread and extras. Pisco sour in Italian restaurant? Fantastic. Really enjoyable, we went very early because we had a show so basically had place to ourselves and we thought it was fantastic. Pricy but to be expected and not out of line for this type.

Met there for a lunch meeting while in NYC.  The service was excellent (there wasn't anyone else in the restaurant until we finished our meal).  The soup was fantastic, pasta was light and homemade and the bread was good.

I got food poisoning at this restaurant.  I had a vegetable, ravioli pasta dish, on their "special" menu, that I thought was a harmless choice, cost $30.00.  Never imagined I would get so sick from such a famous, expensive restaurant !  Never again !  Buyer beware.

I am glad I took my fiend here for her birthday celebration. 

We really enjoyed the ambiance, friendly service and personal attention as well as the food.

We split a seafood appetizer and we each ordered a special pasta dish. Me friend had the fettuccine bolognese, and I had the fettuccine with beal ragu and truffles.  Both delicious and huge.

We also split a botte of Pinot Grigio.

Everything was very good! Would return for other dishes. Classy experience but not overbearing. Waiters were warm and genuine.

We have been eating here and at it's sister restaurant, Cistina, for years. The food usually is very good and the service usually top notch; it's on the pricey side but that's fine. Our last experience, however, assures that we will never go back. We were greeted with a waiter walking around with a magnum of rose Prosecco like a troubador which they were offering to all the tables. It appeared to be one of  those complimentary routines the way he was sauntering around and we accepted although my wife doesn't really drink and I am not a rose fan of any vintage. It was palatable but let's face it, Prosecco is just Prosecco. We then ordered our appetizers and entrees from the "Specials" which were voluminous. The fig and prosciutto appetizer, which we split, was hardly enough for one and only so-so. The entrees were fine, but the bill at the end of the meal was the kicker. The Proseccos were anything but complimentary at $25 a glass which was extraordinary in that they only charged me $18 for a very good glass of Pinot Grigio which I had with the sauteed soft shells and you can get the best bottle of Prosecco for $24 or so. And, while the Branzino, which my wife had, was $50, a not unusual amount for a fish dish in New York, the two small crabs were also $50 per order, a ridiculous price--- I had purchased some a few weeks ago to make at home for $3.25 each. Maybe our fault for not asking the price but they never disclosed them either and that Prosecco routine is just a cheap scam. These are your clients. Why do you want to fool them that way?

Great wine selection. Lovely and knowledgeable bartender. Friendly staff. Stopped here on way home and was not disappointed. You really have to know the place to come otherwise you'll walk right past it and miss it......

I have dined here a dozen times. Food and services is amazing. Prices are high but worth it. Last visit there, a cockroach showed up at our table. Waiter moved us to a new table but just gave us some complimentary cookies to make up for the mishap. I was expecting something befitting having our experience ruined by their lack of proper extermination. Probably won't visit there again.

Restaurant was ok. I don't mind spending top dollar on fine dining but this was certainly far from it (with the exception of the complimentary squash soup, which was divine). I do not recommend as there are numerous other restaurants that you could go to and have a far better experience. Lastly, the meal was painfully slow.

Saturday evening in July after lockdown everyone wants to sit in the middle of the street for vino and cucina Italiana.  An older well-heeled crowd (with masks) sit beneath umbrellaed tables as the army of waiters fill water glasses and arrange bread (fresh!) and olives (lovely but pitted) on tiny tables.  Tasty calamari salad completes the picture. Price$$ are not for the faint of heart.

Our quest asked to go.  So here we are!  
The table they showed us was not under an umbrella and my Dark Sky app is telling me rain in an hour.  So we ask to move in a more protected outside table.  We got a little pushback from Brian but we insisted and were accommodated  I liked the touch of waving to people as they drive by! It adds an unusual twist to a high end dining experience 
We all had a rose champagne to start.  Beautiful 
Prima it's tuna tartar, caprese salad and mushroom ravioli.  All ok nothing impressive 
For main course it's Dover sole for me.  Veal Marsala and Cornish hen.  My son an amateur chef is not impressed with his hen 
But the conversation with our quest is fascinating as usual and time goes by so quickly 
Finally boudino dessert and espresso tops off the culinary experience 
Right on time it starts to rain.  We're safely tucked away under an ample umbrella! Another party is not so lucky! Dark Sky is just so amazing. The maitr'd promptly downloads the app!   
All in all not a spectacular experience but ok given the covid crisis
The food and the service is excellent. Definitely going to come here again. Try their risotto and tiramisu. Its amazing!

It was nice  to have an amuse Bouche again. This high end, expensive nouveau Italian does not fail to please. Disregard the prices, just order freely and enjoy the evening. You will not be rushed. You'll be waited on hand and foot. You'll be taken care of. Of course you'll pay for it. But sometimes it's just worth it. Plenty other Italian places out there. Set an a stopwatch from when you start to when you should end. Not this place.
The bread basket is delicious. I had the veal with truffles in the fontina cheese. My wife had the T-bone. Both were cooked to perfection and enjoyed. I will come back there hopefully with a bigger appetite and dive into their vast selection of non-traditional Italian desserts. Thanks for a wonderful relaxing enjoyable meal with my wife.
Service was great and attentive. Lots of locals and regulars that come here.  Outdoor dining was nice  during Covid.

Nice outside sitting
Food was barely edible 
Wine was definitely turning bad
Service was subpar 
At the prices this place charges, everything should be amazing.

This restaurant saved the day. I'd accidentally made reservations at a different place for the wrong day and I was able to get a seat here last minute. I am so happy I did because everything was spectacular! Andres, our server, was especially kind and welcoming. If you're looking for fine dining italian, I'd definitely recommend you give this place a shot. The veal tortellini was my favorite but everything was great.

Came here for the first time for a lunch and had a great experience. 

Firstly, really nice outdoor dining setup. Was very quiet for a Sunday lunch, but just a really pleasant place for a meal on a nice day. 

Menu was large, but I opted for the carpaccio to start, then the chicken Milanese for my main. The carpaccio was fantastic- I'd go so far as to say it was the best I've ever had. The Milanese was really good as well. 

I tried someone else's pappardelle and bucatini - both were great.

Highly recommend this spot on the UeS

Staff at Caravaggio is a bit out of practice. From pen marks on the table cloth, to forgetting to bring menus, the staff seemed utterly bewildered to have customers. 

Once seated at your table, you are presented with an assortment of breads and butters. The anchovy butter was delicious and reminds you of a brief summer in Porto. 

I recommend reviewing the menu at Caravaggio before making your reservation. They have some unique dishes, for example: lemon-mint-saffron  risotto. While these types of combinations might be appetizing to some, the clash between the mint and saffron might be off-putting to others 

If you want to go classic, that might not help either. Their Bucatini all'Amatriciana was overcooked. The texture of the guanciale gives me a sneaky feeling they boiled it. 

What I did enjoy was their carpaccio served with truffles. This was quite delicious and I would recommend it.

Everything a white linen Italian restaurant should be!!! Delicious food, impeccable service, and classy ambiance. Can't recommend enough. Outside dining: full protocols being implemented. I shall return soon.

Once a shining star on the UPE.  Caravaggio is now a Legend in their own mind- The owner is outrageously arrogant, a terrible stand in chef and doesn't understand what customer service looks likes- his attitude is; if you don't like like, leave. Food is overpriced and inconsistent - it has become a true disappointment.
Magnificent restaurant. Great service atmosphere wine and food. Thought I was back in an elegant restaurant in Rome or Florence.   Highly recommend

We came here for an early dinner and really enjoyed our meal. The cocktails are great (espresso martini and lavender lady). We started with the tuna carpaccio/tuna tartare and loved this. I loved how simple it was and the tuna tartare had so much flavor. I also liked the mix of capers and grapefruit. I didn't think that combination would go with tuna but it went really well. We also got the beef carpaccio which we also loved. We loved how it had truffles on top and fresh pieces of parmesan cheese. We then shared the gnocchi which we really enjoyed and they split it for us. The texture of the gnocchi was soft and fluffy. However, I didn't love the flavor of the red sauce, it almost had a smoky flavor to it. I would definitely come back to try more dishes.

Decided to have an impromptu Saturday lunch al fresco at Caravaggio.  Was not disappointed. If you thought salads were boring, try the exquisite arugula and lettuce salad with hazelnut dressing.  That was my wife's choice.  I began with carpaccio, beautifully sliced, with thin wedges of cheese and capers.  Could not have been improved.  
We then had parchetti with cherry tomatoes, basil and tomato sauce--simple and elegant-- and fettuccini prima vera, with fresh peas, fava beans, tiny cauliflower and other vegetables, in a mild EVO and butter emulsion.  Again, simple and elegant and delicious. For dessert we shared a construction with a chocolate base and pistachio ice cream, studded with tiny meringue kisses and wild strawberries from Malaga and a few tiny candied orange peel juliennes.  It was the pièce de résistance, elaborate and delicious. The service was very friendly and professional. Caravaggio is not a high-end foodie franchise. The chef who gets the credit is actually the chef who makes your meal. Lunch for two with a Bloody Mary, an iced tea and 2 espressos came to $210 with a decent tip. It was worth every penny.

Another gorgeous spring evening in the city. We had reservations for one of our fav Italian spots. Maybe u can't get on a plane to Italy just yet, but you can be there in food, drink & spirit! 
Started w an Aperol Spritz, if that doesn't say party in a glass, nothing does. It was both beautiful & delish, my first one! Started w the green salad & had the fish w morel mushrooms, to die for! Husband had the veal chop: he enjoyed that! 
This whole dining outside thing is great, especially at Caravaggio!

This restaurant is just lovely. The dining room is covered in the most beautiful pink peonies. The staff is super friendly and welcoming. The food is outstanding, my favorite was the Veal Milanese with prosciutto and black truffles!

Fantastic lunch! Spur of moment stopped by last week and seated outside. Amazing and tremendous Frisee salad w chicken livers, could have been lunch. Stuffed zucchini blossoms were just ok, wouldn't order again. Absolutely loved my vitello tonnato! Almost never see it on menu. Would go back just for that! Black ink pasta w seafood also delicious! Wine by the glass (could use more options)  and cocktails are over priced, but that is UES I guess. Honesty would go more often if they had less expensive options. Overall loved the restaurant. Service was professional and courteous too. Attractive outside seating area and inside very attractive. Looking forward to returning!

Casual and distinguished atmosphere, a culinary trip through Italy, I just would like you to improve the quality of your products so that the experience was extraordinary, excellent service, prices for just above the
 Average,  I would like to recommend that you change the coffee  for one that is at the height of this magnificent restaurant, I would like someone to transport me directly to Napoli Italia

Casual y distinguido ambiente, un viaje culinario por Italia, solo me gustaría que mejorara en la calidad de sus productos  para que la experiencia fuese extraordinaria, excelente atención, precios por poco arriba del
Promedio, me gustaría recomendarles que cambien el café  por alguno que esté a la altura de este magnífico restaurante, me gustaría alguno que me transporte directamente a Napoli Italia

This restaurant has very poor service and slow. The waitress was judging us based peoples clothes and because we looked young. Definitely do not recommend!! The staffs are rude! Please don't act high end when the staffs are low class. Do not ever come! The food is not worth it and overpriced

This is hands down one of the best dining experiences and meals I have had in the last 2 years (hard to count 2020- so going back to 2019!) 
The service was AMAZING- so attentive, kind and easy- no pressure, just informative and helpful staff through and through. 

The food is truly why I'm writing this review As every dish we ordered was better than the last. We tried zucchini flowers as an appetizer and loved it. I ordered a truffle pasta and my husband ordered veal Milanese with truffles for dinner and both were fabulous. For the price the serving sizes were quite large and being that we live near by we actually took our leftovers to go- not something I'm in the habit of doing.

There is an outdoor patio but the interior is a beautiful dining room and for dinner I prefer it. Go for a special occasion or date night- take your parents when they're in town visiting or stop for a bite before a show- Caravaggio won't dissapoint- 5 stars all the way.

My gf and I went here for our 4 year anniversary, which we had a reservation for. As soon as we walked in, the host saw my gf in shorts and said we can sit outside, which we thought was odd. Mind you, we were dressed up for the occasion. The manager, who was also our waiter, said it was fine for us to sit in the dining room. The restaurant is beautiful with all the unique art. There was no music, which made it library quiet. The drinks were decent. I got the pomegranate margarita and my gf got the strawberry lemonade mojito. All the food we got was a special: the fig salad, turbot fish, and linguine with tomatoes, mushrooms, and clams. The fig salad was incredible! The turbot and linguine were good, but nothing special considering the priciness of the restaurant. Definitely check out the menu before coming here because it has different food, not really for a picky eater.

Tonight, we took my extended family to what we thought was one of the finest restaurants in New York City. I had emailed a week prior, a picture and specific details for the restaurant to prepare an 80th birthday celebration cake for my mom and our out of town guests. The entire week before I had to call, email and try to get assurance that the cake would be what I had asked for and I was finally assured that it would be after numerous calls and emails. The cake that was brought out bore now resemblance to what we had been promised and it was tasteless. When we approached the manager to express our disappointment, he told us that not only would we have to pay for the cake but that he had no idea what the cake was supposed to be. We were an 8 person party who ordered appetizers, a main course, 4 bottles of wine and a special birthday cake and the manager was incredibly rude and unprofessional. I was mortified that the manager treated my out of town family like this; he should never speak to anyone the way he did let alone a large party that spent over $1500 for a once in a lifetime birthday celebration. Absolutely unacceptable and we will be reaching out to the restaurant owner (who's name the manager would not give) and we will never return. In a city that I have lived in for 20 years and that has a multitude of fine restaurants that are willing to go above and beyond to make their clientele happy, this manager CLEARLY did not care at all my family celebration,  an important birthday that left us with nothing but regret.

The waiting staff was great! But there was a HUGE disconnect with the manager. He refused to remove a dish from the menu that was completely wrong (not what I ordered) and was very rude to my grandparents in the process. Sad to see someone so careless running a restaurant "committed to excellence".

WONDERFUL DESIGN with art that makes you feel as though you're in a collector's apartment. Food is terrific.........but BE CAREFUL as they have a tendency to UP-SELL. Service is terrific too. We'd not been there in years but after last night we'll be back. Dale had strong feelings (unusual) and asked me to write this review. I agree with her.
This place is amazing!! Stumbled upon it after finishing at the Apple Store. The food, ambiance, & service is top notch. Every elegant, food & drinks are amazing!! Great date spot

I came here for lunch with my aunt. Sam was our server and was incredibly attentive and charismatic. The ambiance is warm and inviting, but can get a bit noisy in the back dining room.
I ordered the asparagus salad to start and the vitello tonnato as an entrée. Both were phenomenal.
Excellent service and food. We sat outside which was lovely. Loved the calamari salad. The tiramisu is also excellent.

House martini with blue cheese olives was great! !but on the pricier end... the fettuccine was a little overcooked, the pasta was not Al dente but the flavors were decent, loved the veal and truffle! Bread was a little dry but Service was good.
Update: just look at the owner's response to my review. That's all you need to know. Don't go here!

An upscale Italian
A friendly service
Great food, great wine
Borata, pasta, zucchini flowers
All was great

On my way home after a rough day so even though it was early I decided to stop by and have dinner. Had no reservation so they couldn't seat me outside in their covered area. They offered me a sidewalk table but  rain was imminent so went inside.
Attractive restaurant. Lots of staff. And they pay attention to you but just right-not too much.
Had carpaccio to start with (meh) but the main course I chose, pasta with a very spicy sauce made of sausages etc, was excellent.  Wine by the glass is a decent size. Too full to enjoy desert but their decaf expresso was a perfect way to end the meal.
Not my most favorite restaurant in the neighborhood but perfectly nice.

We had the best meal here. White tablecloths and silver forks. One of the waiters came and recited the entire special menu for about five min - impressive that he could remember all the details. Service was great- no hovering or bossiness, just right. 
My BF had the sesame crusted tuna steak, rare, which is really yummy. Tasty wine and cocktails as well. Probably the best meal out of all our dinners during vacay.

Why on earth would anyone eat here!! I went once and got sick but then thought maybe it was something else so I decided to try it again.. ok lesson learned! Never ever will I go here again! It's absolutely disgusting! Pasta covered in oil and heavy cream.

Awful experience: average food, mediocre drinks and a wrong bill at the end. To which we pointed out and they just ignored the error the waitress made. So we ended up paying more to avoid a scene. Be aware and check each item on your bill!

Fabulous lunch including fig salad, carpacio, octopus, and black fetucini with fish...all terrific...great service and a wonderful dining room...which i would always choose above eating outside...expensive but worth it

MOUSE in the dining room - not well-handled by staff and email not responded to by restaurant. 

Mouse came into the dining room three times during our meal and came right up beside my friend. The staff awkwardly shrugged it off the first time. The second time they walked into that section of the restaurant to scare it away. The third time they didn't even seem to want to know and seemed to be avoiding the dining room. 

I was surprised no manager came over and that none of the staff said anything to suggest this wasn't normal, surprised to be charged full price, and even to be upsold on the dessert wine. My friend was too embarrassed to complain. I emailed the restaurant and got no response. 

I have never seen a live rodent inside a dining room and was pretty shocked by the restaurants lack of any response. Not good.

Have dined here a couple of times but WILL never return. They don't give you a table if you're wearing shorts during the day in the hot NY summer. Btw, the staff is condescending. Byyye, your era is over.

Very nice Italian in a very nice ambience. Extensive wine list, great martinis, and great service. 

We had the Spaghetti Trapanese, Paccheri, and Gnocchi, with a Boston Salad to night. All were great (with the Paccheri particularly notable). 

Will come back soon.

Had a spectacular meal for 6 people here. We doubled the size of our party within the hour of our reservation yet the restaurant accommodated us and treated us royally. Very upscale ambiance and delicious food plus great cocktails. The service was smooth, accommodating and elegant while not feeling fussy. We had two younger kids who found plenty to love on the menu while the adults enjoyed a lovely meal and a delicious Gavi. They took very good care of us and I will definitely return.
love this place is usually sit at the bar and eat and drink. pretty east euro bartender, very attentive.  get the veal

Service: They were very accommodating and nice from the moment we walked in to the moment we left. 
Food: It was amazing, very tasty, very fresh , overall phenomenal taste and presentation. 

*Would 100% recommend it

Wowza!  We live just a few blocks away, but somehow have never been to Caravaggio (perhaps still wanting to hold on to memories of Coco Pazzo?).   Caravaggio ain't cheap, but it's beyond worth it, that's how good it is.  Everyone in our party said that the the first course appetizers/salads were the best ever, and then we all again unanimously said that our main courses were among the best we've every had!  We were stuffed but ended up sharing a souffle, and, we weren't surprised, but another grand slam.  Save up and go, you will not be disappointed!  (I could not understand how Caravaggio didn't have all 5 star reviews, so looked at people who gave it just one star, and saw that one of them gave Applebee's 4 stars, I rest my case!)

Amazing service, amazing food , amazing environment!!! this is a true treat for each one of your senses. From the minute you step through the doors each of your senses is touched, beautifully and intimate way. This is for anyone who wants to grab a nice easy meal or have a full dining experience. The artwork, the attention to detail, every aspect of fine dining is  considered by Chef Guiseppi and his daughter, Nicolina. Caravaggio and sestina are worth a trip itself to New York City. Anyone who lives here I must do!

Great food ! Nice menu, lots of specials. Many options. Beautiful place with art on the walls. Matisse, Frank Stella, one of a kind in NYC. Nice staff, professional, knowledgeable and welcoming. Lunch, dinner or drinks at the bar... always a good experience at Caravaggio !

Caravaggio is an elegant restaurant with delicious food. Everyone is accommodating and professional.  The waitstaff treats us like family and knows our preferred drinks!  It's truly a hidden gem on UES!
Outstanding food and service.  Aleays a great meal at Caravaggio!  You must try it.
Fabulous! The food is excellent but not pretentious. The wine list is TDF and service is old school professional but warm. The room is cosy but not at all cramped. My favourite place in NYC
Excellent food and service.  Nice decor.  Be advised this is a very upscale Upper East Side restaurant, populated by wealthy Upper East Side clientele.  It was not our scene at all.  Very expensive.

This is a ten star restaurant. The food is excellent and the menu varied. The service is impeccable, both friendly and professional. The atmosphere is beautiful with impressibe art throughout the space.
Caravaggio is the sister restaurant of Sistina. When I dont go to Sistina for dinner I will come here. Love having dinner at the bar. Pasta always a great choice.

Caravaggio is an extremely classy place. The food is wonderful, and the service is impeccable. The dining room is warm and inviting with fun, thought-provoking art adorning the elegant space throughout. This is fine dining at its best.
Caravaggio is one of the finest Italian restaurants on the UES. In particular, their gnocchi is out of this world as are all their entrees. Pricey but we'll worth it! Service is outstanding too.

Fabulous food and wonderful service. Food was so fresh and beautifully and deliciously prepared. So good in fact that we went back the next night to take another guest!

Lovely ambiance. Great for hearing each other speak. Staff is so helpful with great recommendations. We will return!
Highly recommend Caravaggio. Great food, friendly and attentive service, and lovely atmosphere.

We have been there many times with friends for dinner and recently for lunch. Celebrated my birthday there. Every time the service is impeccable , excellent food presented beautifully, great wine and drinks, and everything is super clean. Would absolutely recommend for any occasion.
I always find the food here delicious and the service excellent. Its always a memorable dinner.   It's hard to get a reservation at times but worth the wait.
Food and service was exceptionally! A bit pricey, but a good option to have in your pocket whenever you're in the neighborhood.
Amazing experience. Last night, we had a dinner for two and it was unforgettable. A special thanks to Nicolina and all the friendly staff!!
